title: Order of the Court — regular bail
body: In the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh. Criminal Miscellaneous Application No. 4471 of 2026. The petitioner, through counsel, seeks the grant of regular bail in a case registered under Sections 420, 467 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, at Police Station Sector 34, Chandigarh. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has already remained in custody for four months and eleven days, that the investigation stands concluded, and that the challan has been presented before the trial court on the fourteenth of July, 2026. It is further submitted that the recovery, if any, has already been effected, and that the petitioner is neither a previous convict nor involved in any other case of a like nature. The learned State counsel, on the other hand, opposes the prayer and contends that the allegations are grave, that the amount alleged to have been misappropriated is substantial, and that the petitioner, if released, is likely to influence the material witnesses who are yet to be examined. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the custody certificate placed on the record, this Court is of the considered opinion that no useful purpose would be served by keeping the petitioner behind bars during the pendency of the trial, particularly when the challan already stands presented and the recovery is complete. However, the apprehension expressed by the State with regard to the witnesses cannot be brushed aside altogether. Accordingly, the present petition is allowed. The petitioner is ordered to be released on regular bail on his furnishing bail bonds and surety bonds to the satisfaction of the trial court, subject to the following conditions. First, the petitioner shall join the trial on each and every date of hearing, unless his personal presence is specifically exempted. Second, the petitioner shall not, directly or indirectly, tamper with the prosecution evidence or attempt to win over any of the witnesses. Third, the petitioner shall not leave the country without the prior permission of the trial court, and shall deposit his passport, if any, with that court. Fourth, in the event of the petitioner being found to have violated any of the conditions imposed herein, it shall be open to the prosecution to move an appropriate application for the cancellation of bail. It is made clear that nothing observed hereinabove shall be construed as an expression of opinion on the merits of the case, and the observations made are confined to the disposal of the present bail application alone. The petition stands disposed of in the above terms. A copy of this order be sent to the trial court concerned for information and compliance. Ordered accordingly.

title: Office Memorandum — earned leave
body: Subject: Regulation of earned leave and the maintenance of the leave account in respect of the ministerial establishment. Reference: The instructions issued vide this office endorsement No. Estt-II/2026/1187, dated the second of March, 2026, and the rules framed thereunder. The undersigned is directed to invite the attention of all the branch officers and the officials of the ministerial establishment to the subject and the reference cited above, and to convey the following instructions for strict compliance. It has been observed that, in a number of cases, applications for the grant of earned leave are being submitted at the eleventh hour, and often after the leave has already been availed of, which practice is wholly irregular and contrary to the rules on the subject. All the officials are, therefore, informed that an application for earned leave must reach the office of the undersigned at least seven clear days before the date from which the leave is proposed to be availed, save in cases of genuine emergency, the nature of which shall be recorded in writing. The leave account of each official shall be maintained by the dealing hand in the prescribed register, and shall be reconciled at the close of every quarter. No leave shall be treated as sanctioned unless and until a formal order to that effect has been issued by the competent authority. The head of each branch shall ensure that, before forwarding any application, the balance at the credit of the official concerned is duly verified with reference to the entries in the service book. Where an official proceeds on leave without the prior sanction of the competent authority, the period of absence shall, subject to the orders of that authority, be liable to be treated as leave without pay, without prejudice to any disciplinary action that may be warranted. It is further clarified that the sanctioning authority may, in the interest of the public service, refuse, curtail or revoke the leave already sanctioned, and no official shall claim leave as a matter of right. The branch officers are requested to bring these instructions to the notice of every official working under their respective charge, and to obtain their dated signatures in token of having read and understood the same. A compliance report, in the enclosed proforma, shall be furnished to the establishment branch not later than the fifteenth of this month. This issues with the approval of the competent authority. All concerned are expected to adhere to these instructions in letter and in spirit, so that the disposal of the leave applications is regulated in an orderly and timely manner, and the leave accounts are kept up to date at all times.

title: Notice — publication of the daily cause list
body: Notice for the information of the members of the Bar and the general public. It is hereby notified that, with effect from the first working day of the coming month, the daily cause list of this Court shall be published on the official web portal by six o'clock in the evening on the preceding working day, and the practice of circulating printed copies in the branches shall be discontinued in a phased manner. The advocates appearing in the matters listed before the various benches are advised to consult the electronic cause list carefully, and to note the bench, the item number and the approximate time indicated against each case. The matters shall ordinarily be taken up in the serial order in which they appear in the list, subject to such adjustments as the bench concerned may find necessary in the course of the day. Where a matter has been shown as part-heard, it shall be listed at the top of the board of the bench before which it remained part-heard, and shall be taken up before the fresh matters are called out. In cases which are listed for the first time after notice, the counsel are requested to ensure that the process fee and the requisite number of copies have been filed well in advance, so that the issuance of notice is not delayed on account of any office objection. The office objections, if any, are displayed against the concerned items in the cause list itself, and it shall be the responsibility of the counsel to have such objections removed before the date of hearing. The urgent matters which are mentioned before the bench and are directed to be listed shall be included in an additional or supplementary cause list, which shall be published separately on the same portal. The members of the Bar are further informed that any discrepancy noticed in the cause list, whether in the description of the parties, the nature of the matter, or the stage at which it is shown, may be brought to the notice of the deputy registrar (judicial) in writing, so that the necessary correction is carried out at the earliest. The litigants who appear in person are advised to reach the Court well before the commencement of the day's proceedings, and to seek the assistance of the facilitation centre established in the main building for ascertaining the courtroom in which their matter has been listed. This arrangement is being introduced with a view to ensuring transparency, saving paper, and enabling the counsel and the litigants to plan their appearances in an informed manner. All concerned are requested to co-operate in the smooth implementation of this arrangement. Issued under the orders of the competent authority for general information.

title: Summons to the defendant
body: In the Court of the Civil Judge (Senior Division), Chandigarh. Civil Suit No. 812 of 2026, titled as the plaintiff versus the defendant, for the recovery of a sum of money together with interest and costs. To the defendant, resident of House No. 219, Sector 21, Chandigarh. Whereas the plaintiff, named above, has instituted a suit against you for the recovery of the amount described in the plaint, a copy whereof is annexed to this summons, you are hereby summoned to appear before this Court, in person or through a duly instructed pleader, on the nineteenth of October, 2026, at ten o'clock in the forenoon, to answer the claim made against you. You are directed to file your written statement, along with the documents upon which you intend to rely in support of your defence, on or before the said date, and to bring with you, or to send by a pleader, all the documents and witnesses upon whose evidence you propose to rely in support of your case. Take notice that, in default of your appearance on the day and at the hour aforesaid, the suit shall be heard and determined in your absence, and an ex parte decree may be passed against you, which shall be binding upon you in all respects. You are further informed that, should you admit the claim of the plaintiff, either wholly or in part, you may deposit the admitted amount in this Court, and such deposit shall be taken into account at the time of the final adjudication of the suit. If you contend that the claim of the plaintiff is barred by limitation, or that this Court has no jurisdiction to try the suit, or that the plaint is liable to be rejected on any ground available in law, you shall raise such objection specifically in your written statement, and shall not be permitted to raise it at a later stage save with the leave of the Court. It is made clear that a mere denial of the averments contained in the plaint shall not be treated as a sufficient answer, and that you are required to deal specifically with each of the material allegations, admitting, denying or explaining the same, as the case may be. The plaintiff has valued the suit for the purposes of court fee and jurisdiction at the amount stated in the plaint, and the requisite court fee stands affixed thereon. Given under my hand and the seal of this Court, on this the seventh day of September, in the year two thousand and twenty-six. By order of the Court, the reader is directed to ensure due service of this summons upon the defendant in accordance with law.

title: Judgment — regular second appeal
body: This regular second appeal has been preferred by the defendant against the judgment and decree passed by the learned lower appellate court, whereby the appeal filed by the plaintiff was accepted, the judgment of the trial court was set aside, and the suit for possession by way of specific performance of the agreement to sell was decreed in favour of the plaintiff. The facts, in brief, are that the plaintiff instituted a suit for specific performance on the averment that the defendant had entered into an agreement to sell the suit property for a stated consideration, that a substantial part of the sale consideration was paid at the time of the execution of the agreement, and that the defendant, despite repeated requests and a legal notice, failed to execute the sale deed within the stipulated period. The defendant contested the suit and denied the execution of the agreement, and pleaded, in the alternative, that the plaintiff was never ready and willing to perform his part of the contract. The trial court, on an appreciation of the evidence, dismissed the suit, holding that the plaintiff had failed to prove his readiness and willingness. The lower appellate court, however, reversed those findings and decreed the suit. At the time of the admission of this appeal, the following substantial question of law was framed, namely, whether the lower appellate court was justified in reversing the well-reasoned findings of the trial court without adverting to the material evidence on the record. Having heard learned counsel for the parties at some length, and having carefully examined the record, this Court finds that the lower appellate court, being the final court of fact, has recorded cogent reasons for its conclusions, and has dealt with each item of the evidence led by the parties. The readiness and willingness of the plaintiff has been established not merely by his own statement, but also by the surrounding circumstances, including the part payment made and the conduct of the plaintiff in issuing the legal notice within a reasonable time. The concurrent appreciation of the documentary evidence does not disclose any perversity or misreading which would warrant interference in the exercise of the limited jurisdiction available to this Court in a second appeal. It is well settled that this Court is not to reappreciate the evidence as though it were sitting as a first appellate court, and that a finding of fact, howsoever erroneous, cannot be disturbed unless it is shown to be perverse or based on no evidence. No such infirmity having been pointed out, the substantial question of law framed is answered against the appellant. Consequently, the appeal, being devoid of merit, is dismissed, and the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court are affirmed. The parties are left to bear their own costs throughout.

title: Affidavit of the deponent
body: Affidavit of the deponent, aged about forty-two years, son of the late resident of Sector 15, Panchkula, presently working as a clerk in the establishment branch. I, the deponent above-named, do hereby solemnly affirm and declare as under. That I am the applicant in the accompanying application, and am fully conversant with the facts and circumstances of the case, and am therefore competent to swear this affidavit. That the facts stated in the accompanying application may kindly be read as an integral part of this affidavit, and are not being reproduced herein for the sake of brevity, so as to avoid unnecessary repetition. That I have not concealed any material fact from this Court, and that whatever has been stated in the application is true and correct to the best of my knowledge, and nothing material has been kept back or misstated. That the documents annexed to the application are true copies of their respective originals, the originals whereof are in my possession and shall be produced before this Court as and when so directed. That I have not filed any other application or petition, either before this Court or before any other court or authority, seeking the same or a similar relief, and that no such matter is pending anywhere. That the present application has been filed bona fide and in the interest of justice, and not with any intention to delay the proceedings or to cause any prejudice to the opposite party. That I undertake to abide by such orders and directions as this Court may deem fit to pass in the matter, and to render such assistance to the Court as may be required for the just adjudication of the controversy. That the deponent craves the leave of this Court to place on the record such further documents and facts as may become necessary during the course of the hearing, and to amend or supplement the averments made herein, if the occasion so arises. Verification. Verified at Chandigarh, on this the seventh day of September, two thousand and twenty-six, that the contents of the above affidavit are true and correct to the best of my knowledge and belief, that no part thereof is false, and that nothing material has been concealed therefrom. The contents have been read over and explained to me in the vernacular, which I have understood, and I have signed this affidavit in token of the correctness thereof. The deponent has been identified by the counsel appearing in the matter, who is personally known to the deponent, and whose signatures are appended below in the presence of the attesting officer. I make this solemn affirmation, believing the same to be true, and knowing that, if the statements made herein are found to be false, I shall be liable to be proceeded against in accordance with law.

title: Office note — forwarding for orders
body: Note for the kind consideration and orders of the competent authority, submitted through the proper channel. The matter relates to the representation dated the twenty-third of August, 2026, received from an official of the ministerial establishment, wherein he has requested that the period spent by him on deputation be counted towards the qualifying service for the purposes of the grant of the next higher pay scale under the assured career progression scheme. The relevant record has been examined in this branch, and the position is placed below for the perusal of the competent authority. The official concerned joined the service on the eleventh of June, 2011, and was sent on deputation to a subordinate office on the second of January, 2018, from which deputation he stood reverted on the thirtieth of September, 2021. As per the instructions on the subject, the period spent on deputation to an equivalent post is ordinarily to be counted towards the qualifying service, provided that the deputation was sanctioned by the competent authority and the requisite contributions, if any, stand recovered. On a scrutiny of the service book, it is found that the deputation was duly sanctioned vide the order noted in the margin, and that there is no adverse entry on the record which would disentitle the official to the benefit claimed. It is, however, observed that the pension contribution in respect of a part of the deputation period is yet to be reconciled with the accounts branch, and a reference in this regard is being processed separately. In view of the foregoing, it is respectfully submitted that the case appears to be covered by the instructions on the subject, and that the benefit sought may be admissible, subject to the reconciliation of the contribution referred to above. The draft of the sanction order, if approved, is placed on the flag for signatures. It is further submitted, for the information of the competent authority, that a similar representation from another official is under examination in this branch, and that a consolidated position in respect of all such cases shall be put up in due course, so as to ensure uniformity in the treatment of these matters. The file is, accordingly, submitted for such orders as the competent authority may be pleased to pass. Should the authority so desire, the dealing hand may be directed to obtain the reconciliation from the accounts branch before the sanction is issued, so that the order, when passed, is complete in all respects and does not require any subsequent amendment. Submitted, please, for orders. Put up on the noting side after the orders have been obtained, for the issuance of the necessary communication to the official concerned.

title: Notification — computer proficiency test
body: It is notified for the information of all the candidates who have qualified in the written examination for the post of Clerk that the computer proficiency test, which is the qualifying practical stage of the recruitment, shall be conducted in accordance with the schedule and the criteria set out hereunder. The candidates are advised to read the following instructions carefully, and to note that any deviation from the instructions may render a candidate liable to have his candidature cancelled. The computer proficiency test shall consist of two papers, namely, a test of English typing and a practical test in the use of a spreadsheet, and both the papers shall be of a qualifying nature only, the marks whereof shall not be added to the marks obtained in the written examination for the purpose of preparing the final merit list. In the typing test, each candidate shall be required to reproduce, within the time allowed, a printed passage handed over to him in the examination hall, and the speed shall be computed after making the deductions prescribed for the mistakes committed, the candidate being required to attain the minimum speed notified for the post. In the spreadsheet test, each candidate shall be required to enter the data supplied to him, to apply the formulae indicated in the question paper, to prepare the chart called for, and to save the work under the name specified, the whole of the exercise being marked out of the total prescribed, with a separate minimum for qualifying. The candidates shall report at the examination centre at the time indicated in their admit cards, which shall be an hour before the commencement of the session, and no candidate shall be permitted to enter the hall after the session has begun. The candidates shall bring with them the admit card and one original photo identity document, and shall not carry any mobile telephone, calculator, printed matter or writing material into the examination hall, all such articles being liable to be deposited outside the hall at the risk of the candidate. The machines and the software installed at the centre shall be provided by the commission, and the candidates shall satisfy themselves, at the commencement of the session, that the machine allotted to them is functioning properly, any defect being reported to the invigilator forthwith. The candidates are warned that the use of any unfair means, or the causing of any disturbance in the hall, shall be viewed seriously, and shall entail such action as the commission may deem fit, including the cancellation of the candidature and debarment from future examinations. The result of the computer proficiency test shall be published on the official web portal in due course, and no separate intimation shall be sent to any candidate. The candidates are advised to keep visiting the portal for further information. Issued by order of the commission for general information and strict compliance.
